definition: Recording every run's config, code version, data version, metrics, and artifacts (W&B, MLflow) so results are comparable and reproducible.
details: Recording every run's config, code version, data version, metrics, and artifacts (W&B, MLflow) so results are comparable and reproducible. The lab notebook of ML teams; its absence is how organizations lose knowledge of why the shipped model works.

explainer.lead: Experiment tracking is the practice of keeping a structured record of every machine-learning run and what it produced. It lets a team compare results fairly and retrace the steps behind a model instead of relying on memory or scattered notes.

tiers.eli5: It is like writing down every time you bake cookies: the recipe, ingredients, oven settings, and how they tasted. When one batch turns out best, you can see exactly what you did and try it again.
tiers.practitioner: For each run, log its configuration, code and data versions, metrics, and artifacts, typically with W&B or MLflow. Use those records to compare candidates and reconstruct the run behind a shipped model; unlogged manual changes and missing data versions weaken that history.
tiers.paperLevel: A tracked run can be represented as r = (c, k, d, m, a), where c is configuration, k is code version, d is data version, m is metrics, and a is artifacts. Recording these fields supports run comparison and reproducibility, although keeping the records does not by itself establish that two runs differ only in the intended way.

explainer.example: A team trains a model with a learning rate of 0.001 and records code version k12, data version d7, an accuracy metric of 0.91, and the saved model artifact. A later run changes only the learning rate to 0.01 and reaches 0.87, giving the team a clear basis for comparison and a record of the better setup.

usedIn.name: Machine-learning teams
usedIn.detail: Used as a shared lab notebook for understanding and reconstructing model results.

explainer.intuition: A model result is not useful on its own if nobody knows which settings, code, and data produced it. Experiment tracking turns each run into a findable, comparable record.
howItWorks: Capture the run's configuration before or as it executes.
Record the code version and data version used.
Store the resulting metrics and artifacts with that run.
Compare recorded runs and use the selected record to reconstruct its setup.
explainer.whyItMatters: It preserves the reasoning and evidence behind model choices, making results comparable and reproducible. Without it, an organization can lose the knowledge of why its shipped model works.
misconceptions: Saving only the final metrics is enough; without configurations and versions, the numbers are difficult to interpret or reproduce.
Tracking is just a results dashboard; its core purpose is to preserve a complete record of each run.

diagram.caption: Each run's setup and outputs are stored together so later runs can be compared and earlier setups reconstructed.
